Yes, you can insert an external video link into your Qualtrics survey, and this should work even if your account restricts HTML embedding.

How to insert your YouTube link

  1. Open your Qualtrics survey.

  2. Add a Text / Graphic question.

  3. Type: Please watch the following 30-second video before proceeding.

  4. Highlight the text Click here to watch the video.

  5. Open the Rich Content Editor and click the link icon.

  6. Paste your URL:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HAB-KaymzXQ

  1. If available, select Open in New Window/Tab.

For your randomized experiment

You can still randomly assign respondents to four conditions, with a different video link for each condition.

But there are two methodological limitations:

  • Treatment exposure: You cannot reliably confirm whether respondents actually watched the video.

  • Timing: A 30-second Qualtrics timer starts when the survey page loads, not when the respondent clicks the external video link.

My recommendation

If your research only requires respondents to be shown the video, an external link may be sufficient.

If your experiment requires controlled exposure to the video before answering subsequent questions, an external link is a weaker solution.

One question: Is your main requirement that participants cannot proceed to the next question until 30 seconds have passed, or that they must actually finish watching the video?

These require different technical solutions.

I need to redirect them back to the survey once they have watched the video. How do I do that

ChatGPT said:ChatGPT

You can redirect respondents back to Qualtrics after watching a video, but there is one important limitation:

YouTube does not provide a built-in feature to automatically return viewers to an external Qualtrics survey when a video finishes.

For your experiment, there are two practical approaches.

Option 1: Open YouTube in a new tab (easiest)

This is the simplest workaround that doesn't require additional Qualtrics permissions.

  1. In Qualtrics, create a Text / Graphic question.

  2. Add the text: Click here to watch the 30-second video.

  3. Hyperlink it to your YouTube video.

  4. Enable Open in New Window/Tab, if available.

  5. Add a Timing question to the same survey page and delay the Next button for 30 seconds.

  6. Add an instruction telling respondents to return to the survey tab after the video finishes.

This keeps the original Qualtrics survey open, so respondents can return without losing their progress.

However, the return is manual, and the 30-second timer does not establish whether they watched the video.

Option 2: Automatic return after the video ends

For a fully automatic experience, you would need a custom video webpage, rather than a normal YouTube watch page.

Qualtrics survey

Respondent assigned to Condition A/B/C/D

External video webpage

Video plays for 30 seconds

Return to Qualtrics

Continue with post-video questions

The external webpage would detect when the video ends and redirect respondents to a continuation link. To preserve the same survey response, the return URL must be designed carefully; simply reopening the survey's anonymous link may start a new response.

Also, Qualtrics' built-in Redirect to URL feature works when respondents finish a survey, not when they finish watching an external video.

Qualtrics

My recommendation

For your research experiment, Option 1 is easier and safer for preserving responses. Option 2 is possible but requires custom webpage hosting and a tested survey-resumption mechanism.

However, there's one important technical issue: returning respondents to the same Qualtrics response is not guaranteed simply by redirecting them to the original survey URL.

Proposed setup

1. Qualtrics

Randomly assign respondent to one of four conditions

2. External video page

Play assigned video and detect completion

3. Return to survey

Resume post-video questions using a validated continuation mechanism

The webpage can use YouTube's Player API to detect the video ending. We can host it for free using GitHub Pages or Netlify. Autoplay may be blocked by browsers, so respondents might need to press Play.

Two ways to handle the Qualtrics return

Approach A — Single survey: Keep Qualtrics open in the original tab, open the video page in another tab, and attempt to return focus to the survey when playback ends. This preserves the original survey session but automatic tab switching isn't guaranteed.

Approach B — Two linked surveys: Use one Qualtrics survey for randomization and a second for post-video questions. The video webpage redirects to the second survey with a unique participant identifier and assigned condition. This enables automatic navigation but requires linking the two response records.

For your research experiment, Approach B is more reliable if automatic redirection is essential.

Google for Developers

2. Host the webpage for free

I recommend GitHub Pages.

  1. Go to GitHub — Create repository.

  2. Create a public repository called qualtrics-video.

  3. Upload the HTML file I provided.

  4. Rename the uploaded file to index.html.

  5. Go to Settings → Pages.

  6. Under Build and deployment, select Deploy from a branch, then choose main and / (root).

  7. Save and wait for deployment.

Your webpage URL will follow this format:

https://YOUR-USERNAME.github.io/qualtrics-video/

Open it to verify that the video plays.

3. Connect the webpage to Qualtrics

In your existing Qualtrics survey:

  1. Add a Text / Graphic question where the video should appear.

  2. Enter: Please click the link below to watch the video before continuing with the survey.

  3. Add the text Watch the video and highlight it.

  4. Click Rich Content Editor → Link.

  5. Paste your GitHub Pages URL.

  6. Under Target, select New Window (_blank), if available.

  7. Save and preview the survey.

Qualtrics documents the New Window option, although changing link targets can require HTML permissions.

Critical: The link must open a new tab. If it replaces the Qualtrics tab, this design will not reliably preserve the original session.

4. Test the complete respondent journey

  1. Respondent opens Qualtrics

    Completes initial questions and reaches the video link.

  2. Respondent opens the video webpage

    The Qualtrics survey stays open in the original tab.

  3. Respondent watches the video

    The webpage detects when YouTube reports playback has ended.

  4. Webpage attempts to return to Qualtrics

    If the browser blocks automatic switching, the respondent uses the return button or selects the original tab.

  5. Respondent continues the same survey

    The existing Qualtrics session remains available in the original tab.

5. Important limitations for your experiment

This setup does not guarantee automatic tab switching, prevent video seeking, or stop respondents from clicking Next in Qualtrics before finishing the video. It also does not automatically record video completion in your Qualtrics response data.

For a research experiment, I recommend adding a simple confirmation question after the video link and piloting the complete flow on desktop and mobile before collecting responses.

The HTML page itself does not require Qualtrics HTML or JavaScript permissions because the video player runs on GitHub Pages, not inside Qualtrics.
